problem_pages.title: Stop Missing Customer Calls
problem_pages.meta_description: Home services businesses miss 30-50% of inbound calls. Every missed call is a lost job. Here's how to catch every one without hiring an office manager.
problem_pages.hero: You're losing $2,000+ a month to missed calls. Here's how to stop.
problem_pages.subhead: The average home services business misses 30-50% of inbound calls. Each one is a $200-500 job walking to your competitor. You don't need to hire someone — you need a system.

sections.heading: The math on missed calls
sections.body:
You're on a roof, under a sink, or behind a pressure washer. The phone rings. You can't answer. The customer calls the next name on Google. You don't even know it happened.

If you get 40 calls a week and miss 15 of them, that's 60 missed calls a month. At $300 average job value, you're leaving $18,000 on the table — every month. Not because your work isn't good. Because you couldn't get to the phone.

sections.heading: Why voicemail doesn't work
sections.body:
Less than 20% of callers leave a voicemail. The rest hang up and call someone else. They're not going to wait for a callback — they need the job done and they'll go with whoever answers first.

This is especially true for urgent calls. A homeowner with a clogged gutter in a rainstorm isn't leaving a message. They're calling the next company.

sections.heading: The fix isn't hiring — it's a system
sections.body:
A part-time office person costs $2,000-3,000 a month, calls in sick, takes vacations, and still can't work nights or weekends. A system that answers every call, captures the lead, gives a price range, and texts you the details — that costs a fraction and works 24/7.

We build these systems custom for home services businesses. Every call is answered in your business's voice, with your services and pricing. The caller thinks they're talking to your office.

faqs.question: How many calls does a typical home services business miss?
faqs.answer: Industry data shows 30-50% of inbound calls go unanswered for small service businesses. During peak season and after hours, that number is even higher.

faqs.question: What happens when someone calls and I can't answer?
faqs.answer: Our system picks up automatically, greets the caller with your business name, finds out what they need, gives a price range, and offers to book an estimate. You get a text with all the details within 30 seconds.

faqs.question: Will callers know they're not talking to a person?
faqs.answer: The system sounds natural and conversational. It knows your services, your pricing, and your service area. Most callers think they're speaking with your office staff.

faqs.question: Does it work after hours and on weekends?
faqs.answer: 24/7, 365 days a year. The calls that come in at 9pm on Saturday — those are the ones your competitors are missing too.

problem_pages.title: How to Follow Up on Quotes Without Chasing
problem_pages.meta_description: 80% of home services quotes never get a follow-up. Automated follow-ups at day 3 and 7 close more jobs without you thinking about it.
problem_pages.hero: 80% of your quotes never get a follow-up. That's money walking away.
problem_pages.subhead: You drove out, looked at the job, gave a fair price. Then you got busy. The customer forgot. The job went to someone who followed up. Sound familiar?

sections.heading: The follow-up gap
sections.body:
Most contractors give a quote and wait for the phone to ring. When it doesn't, they move on. But the customer wasn't saying no — they were busy too. They meant to call back. They forgot.

A simple follow-up at day 3 — just checking in, no pressure — converts 20-30% of quotes that would otherwise go cold. A second touch at day 7 catches even more. Most of your competitors never follow up once. You'd follow up every time.

sections.heading: What good follow-up looks like
sections.body:
Not a sales call. Not a pushy text. A natural, friendly message: 'Hey, just checking in on that driveway quote from last week. Spring's filling up fast — want me to get you on the schedule?'

That's it. Short, personal, low-pressure. The kind of message a great office manager would send — except it happens automatically for every single quote.

sections.heading: Automatic, not annoying
sections.body: We schedule follow-ups at day 3 and day 7 after every quote. If the customer books before then, the follow-ups cancel automatically. If they've gone quiet, the system nudges them. If they say no, it stops. No one gets spammed. Everyone gets remembered.

faqs.question: How many follow-ups should I send?
faqs.answer: Two is the sweet spot — day 3 and day 7. Enough to stay top of mind without being annoying. If the customer hasn't responded after two follow-ups, they're probably not interested right now.

faqs.question: What if the customer already booked?
faqs.answer: Follow-ups cancel automatically when a customer books. The system tracks lead status so nobody gets a 'still interested?' message after they've already scheduled.

faqs.question: Can I customize the follow-up messages?
faqs.answer: Yes. The messages are written in your voice and match how you communicate with customers. We set this up during onboarding so everything sounds natural.

problem_pages.title: Get More Google Reviews for Your Home Services Business
problem_pages.meta_description: More reviews means more calls from Google. Automatically ask every happy customer for a review after every job — without the awkward ask.
problem_pages.hero: More reviews = more calls. Here's how to get them without asking.
problem_pages.subhead: Google reviews are the number one thing potential customers look at before they call. But most service businesses get 1-2 reviews a month because nobody remembers to ask. We fix that.

sections.heading: Why reviews matter more than ever
sections.body:
When someone Googles 'pressure washing near me,' Google shows three results on the map. The businesses with the most (and best) reviews get those spots. Everyone else is invisible.

A business with 50 reviews beats a business with 12 reviews — even if the work quality is identical. Reviews are your digital word of mouth, and most of your competitors aren't systematically collecting them.

sections.heading: The timing is everything
sections.body:
The best time to ask for a review is right after you've done great work. The customer just watched you transform their driveway — they're impressed, they're happy, and they'd gladly say something nice if someone just made it easy.

Our system sends a thank-you text with a direct link to your Google review page 24 hours after every completed job. No awkward asking. No forgetting. Just a simple, well-timed message that gets results.

sections.heading: Respond to every review
sections.body:
Getting reviews is half the equation. Responding to them is the other half. Businesses that respond to reviews get 12% more calls from Google.

We monitor your reviews and draft responses — a quick thank-you for five-star reviews, a thoughtful reply for anything less. You approve before it posts. Your profile stays active and professional.

faqs.question: How many more reviews can I expect?
faqs.answer: Most businesses go from 1-2 reviews per month to 6-10 — just by asking consistently after every job.

faqs.question: What if I get a negative review?
faqs.answer: We draft a professional, empathetic response for you to approve. Responding thoughtfully to criticism actually builds trust with future customers who read your reviews.

faqs.question: Is it okay to ask customers for reviews?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Google explicitly allows and encourages businesses to ask customers for reviews. You just can't offer incentives for them.

problem_pages.title: How to Keep Customers Coming Back
problem_pages.meta_description: Your past customers are your most valuable asset. Recurring reminders, seasonal campaigns, and upsells bring them back automatically.
problem_pages.hero: Your past customers are a goldmine. Stop ignoring them.
problem_pages.subhead: You've done great work for hundreds of people. Most would hire you again — if anyone reminded them. We make sure they never forget about you.

sections.heading: The easiest revenue you'll ever earn
sections.body:
Acquiring a new customer costs 5-7x more than keeping an existing one. Your past customers already trust you, already know your quality, and already have your number somewhere. They just need a reason to call.

Twelve months after a window cleaning, a simple text — 'Hey, it's about that time again' — brings them back. No advertising cost. No competing on price. Just a relationship that keeps paying off.

sections.heading: Seasonal campaigns that run themselves
sections.body:
Every home services business has seasonal patterns. Gutter cleaning in fall. Pressure washing in spring. Holiday lights in September. We build campaigns for each season that reach the right customers at the right time.

Your spring push goes to customers who haven't booked in 6+ months. Your holiday lighting campaign goes out in September before you sell out. All automatic, all personalized.

sections.heading: Upsells that feel natural
sections.body: Had their driveway done but never got their windows cleaned? We reach out: 'A lot of our customers do windows and driveway together — want a quote?' It's not a hard sell. It's a helpful suggestion from a business they already trust.

faqs.question: How do recurring reminders work?
faqs.answer: We track when each customer last had service. When it's time — 12 months for windows, 18 months for driveways, etc. — they get a friendly reminder. Each service type has its own interval.

faqs.question: Can I run seasonal promotions?
faqs.answer: Yes. We set up campaigns for each season during onboarding. Fall gutter cleaning, spring pressure washing, holiday lighting — each targets the right customers at the right time.

faqs.question: What if a customer wants to stop hearing from us?
faqs.answer: They can reply STOP at any time and they're immediately removed from all outreach. We respect that completely.

problem_pages.title: How to Compete With Cheaper Contractors
problem_pages.meta_description: New contractors flooding your market with low prices? Here's how to win on quality, reputation, and professionalism — not price.
problem_pages.hero: They're cheaper. You're better. Here's how to prove it.
problem_pages.subhead: New operators are flooding the market with discount prices and zero experience. You can't beat them on price — and you shouldn't try. Here's how to win anyway.

sections.heading: Price shoppers aren't your customers
sections.body:
The homeowner who picks the cheapest quote every time isn't your ideal customer. They'll haggle, complain, and leave you a bad review over $20. Let them go to the guy with a garden hose and a dream.

Your customers are homeowners who care about their property. They want someone experienced, insured, and reliable. They'll pay more for someone they trust. Your job is making that trust visible before they ever call.

sections.heading: Professionalism is your competitive advantage
sections.body:
When a potential customer calls your competitor, it goes to voicemail. When they call you, a professional voice answers immediately, knows your services and pricing, and books an estimate on the spot. They get a confirmation email within seconds.

Before the competitor even calls them back, you've already made a first impression that says 'this is a real business.' That's worth more than any price discount.

sections.heading: Reviews tell the story for you
sections.body: A cheap contractor with 3 reviews can't compete with an experienced pro with 50 five-star reviews. Every review is a customer vouching for your quality. We make sure every happy customer gets asked, every review gets a response, and your reputation grows month over month.

sections.heading: Be everywhere they search
sections.body: When someone Googles 'pressure washing Walnut Creek,' are you showing up? The cheap operators don't invest in their online presence. A professional website with location-specific pages, reviews, and real content puts you in front of customers who are willing to pay for quality.

faqs.question: How do I justify higher prices to customers?
faqs.answer: You don't justify — you demonstrate. Professional call handling, instant confirmations, follow-ups, and a strong review profile all signal quality. Customers who see that are willing to pay more because they trust you'll do the job right.

faqs.question: Should I lower my prices to compete?
faqs.answer: No. Competing on price is a race to the bottom. Instead, compete on professionalism, responsiveness, and reputation. The customers worth having will pay for quality.

problem_pages.title: Automate Appointment Reminders for Your Service Business
problem_pages.meta_description: Reduce no-shows and look more professional with automatic appointment confirmations and day-before reminders. No more phone tag.
problem_pages.hero: No more no-shows. No more phone tag.
problem_pages.subhead: Appointment confirmations go out instantly. Day-before reminders go out automatically. Rain in the forecast? We reschedule proactively. Your schedule runs itself.

sections.heading: Confirmations that make you look professional
sections.body: When a customer books an estimate, they get a professional confirmation email within seconds — service, date, time, address. Your competitors are texting back 4 hours later from a personal cell phone. You look like a real operation because you are one.

sections.heading: Reminders that prevent no-shows
sections.body: The day before every appointment, your customer gets a reminder. This alone cuts no-shows dramatically. A no-show doesn't just waste your time — it wastes a slot that could have gone to a paying customer.

sections.heading: Weather-aware scheduling
sections.body: Rain in the forecast for your outdoor jobs? The system flags it and reaches out to the customer proactively: 'Looks like rain Thursday — can we move you to Friday morning?' You handle it the night before instead of scrambling at 6am.

faqs.question: Do customers get both a confirmation and a reminder?
faqs.answer: Yes. Confirmation goes out immediately when they book. Reminder goes out the day before the appointment.

faqs.question: What if a customer needs to reschedule?
faqs.answer: They can reply to the reminder to reschedule. The system handles the change and notifies you.

faqs.question: Does this work for estimates and actual jobs?
faqs.answer: Both. Any appointment in the system — whether it's a free estimate or a booked job — gets confirmations and reminders.

problem_pages.title: How to Grow a Home Services Business in 2026
problem_pages.meta_description: The complete guide to growing a home services business: capture every lead, close more quotes, earn more reviews, and keep customers coming back.
problem_pages.hero: The complete playbook for growing your service business.
problem_pages.subhead: More leads, more bookings, more reviews, more repeat customers. Not by working harder — by building systems that do the work for you.

sections.heading: Step 1: Capture every lead
sections.body: Growth starts with not losing what you already have. If you're missing 30-50% of inbound calls, fixing that alone could double your revenue. Every call answered, every lead captured, every inquiry responded to — that's the foundation.

sections.heading: Step 2: Close more of what you quote
sections.body: Getting leads is half the equation. Converting them is the other half. Systematic follow-ups at day 3 and day 7 turn cold quotes into booked jobs. Most contractors give a quote and hope. You follow up every time.

sections.heading: Step 3: Earn reviews that bring more calls
sections.body: Google reviews are the growth engine for local businesses. Every five-star review makes the next customer more likely to call. Systematically asking after every job compounds your reputation over time.

sections.heading: Step 4: Keep customers for life
sections.body: A customer who comes back every year for window cleaning is worth 10x more than a one-time driveway job. Recurring reminders, seasonal campaigns, and thoughtful upsells turn one-time customers into lifetime relationships.

sections.heading: Step 5: Be findable
sections.body: The best business in town loses to the most visible business in town. A professional website with location-specific pages, reviews, and real content puts you in front of customers actively looking for your services.

faqs.question: What's the fastest way to grow my service business?
faqs.answer: Stop losing what you already have. Most businesses can grow 20-30% just by catching missed calls and following up on quotes — without spending a dollar on advertising.

faqs.question: Do I need to spend money on advertising?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Fixing your lead capture, follow-up, and review systems often generates more growth than advertising — because you're converting leads you're already getting.

sections.heading: Generic vs custom

Off-the-shelf answering services give every business the same robot. It doesn't know your services, your pricing, your service area, or how you talk to customers. Callers can tell.

We sit down with you, learn your business, and build a system that knows everything your best office manager would know. It quotes your real prices, covers your real service area, and sounds like someone who actually works for you.

sections.heading: More than answering — operating

An answering service catches the call. That's it. Our system catches the call AND follows up on the quote, books the appointment, sends the confirmation, reminds the customer, asks for the review, and brings them back next year.

You're not paying for someone to pick up the phone. You're paying for someone to run your customer operations.

sections.heading: What it costs vs what it saves

faqs.question: How is this different from Smith.ai or Ruby?
faqs.answer: Those services use live humans or generic AI to answer calls. They don't know your business. We build a custom system trained on your specific services, pricing, and personality — plus we handle everything after the call too.

faqs.question: What about Goodcall or other AI receptionists?
faqs.answer: Self-serve AI receptionists give you a generic template. You configure it yourself (or don't, because you're busy). We handle everything — setup, customization, ongoing optimization. And our system does far more than answer calls.

faqs.question: What if something goes wrong?
